architecture.mechanism: Using anisotropic colloidal particles that form colloidal monolayer membranes (CMMs) with increased bending rigidity to achieve uniform deposition on a substrate surface, leveraging particle shape-induced effects during evaporative assembly to create a protective coating layer.
architecture.intervention: Apply a spray-on hydrocolloidal protective coating containing engineered ellipsoidal nanoparticles onto the leading-edge surface of wind turbine blades during scheduled service windows; as the solvent evaporates, the anisotropic particles self-assemble into a dense, uniform colloidal monolayer membrane with high bending rigidity, forming a durable protective shield against rain and hail impact without requiring any rotor geometry changes.
architecture.expected_effect: A uniformly deposited, mechanically robust nanoparticle coating on the blade leading edge that absorbs and distributes rain/hail impact energy, reducing erosion rates on the underlying composite material and mitigating the 4–6% annual energy production loss caused by surface degradation.
architecture.falsification_test: Apply the ellipsoidal-particle colloidal coating to test blade specimens and subject them to standardized rain/hail erosion testing; if the erosion depth and surface damage metrics are statistically indistinguishable from uncoated control samples after equivalent exposure, the proposed mechanism is not effective under these conditions.
